questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “Draught” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The channel was dredged to five metres, and the coasters that had worked the port for a century could still use it. choices.label: A

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?

questions.passage: Deaf children in Nicaragua were taught at home in isolation until new schools brought several hundred of them together at the end of the 1970s. choices.content: It questions whether the older pupils were signing at all.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It explains why the children had previously been taught at home.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It describes the recording methods the linguists used.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Iceland had lost most of its woodland within a century of settlement, and bare stone holds no heat. Builders raised their walls instead from blocks of turf cut in a herringbone pattern and stacked with the grass still living in them. <u>A wall built this way settles as the turf beneath compresses, so the roof timbers — scarce, salvaged, often driftwood — had to be taken down and reset every few decades.</u> Houses were rebuilt on the same spot so often that the mound under an old farm can be several metres deep.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It explains why woodland disappeared from Iceland after settlement.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It argues that turf was a poorer building material than stone.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It describes the way turf blocks were cut for the walls.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The leading edge of an owl's outermost primary carries a row of stiff combs, the trailing edge is fringed into separate filaments, and the upper surface is covered in a velvet pile. Each of the three breaks up the sheet of turbulent air that would otherwise roll off the wing and hiss. Recordings place the sound of an owl's wingbeat below the hearing threshold of the mice it hunts. Fast owls that take insects on the wing in open air have none of the three.

choices.label: A
choices.content: All owls fly more quietly than other birds of comparable size.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The velvet pile on the wing keeps an owl warm in cold weather.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Three feather structures work to quiet an owl's wing rather than to make its flight faster.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Owls hear considerably better than the mice on which they prey.

questions.stem: According to the text, how is a shortage of water handled?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An acequia is a ditch and also the body of people whose fields it waters. The mayordomo sets the rotation, and every household owes days of labour on the annual cleaning in proportion to the water it draws. In a dry year the shortage is shared rather than allocated by seniority: every turn is shortened by the same fraction. Villages that have run the same ditch for three centuries have put almost none of this in writing.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Every household's turn is cut back so that the shortfall falls on all of them.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The mayordomo buys water from a neighbouring ditch association.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Households that supplied the most labour receive the most water.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Water goes first to the households holding the oldest rights.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Aalto's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A wood frog in midwinter has ice between its organs, no heartbeat and no measurable breathing, and thaws in spring without injury. Physiologist Karin Aalto argues that survival depends on the frog flooding its cells with glucose before the freeze rather than on any inherent toughness of the tissues.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Wood frogs range further north than any other North American frog.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Frozen wood frogs can be thawed and refrozen several times in one winter.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Frogs whose livers were blocked from releasing glucose died at temperatures that untreated frogs survived unharmed.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Wood frogs begin to freeze at a higher temperature than most other amphibians do.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ferrand's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The cheeses ripen in caves in a limestone scree, where cool air moves constantly through the fissures. Cheesemaker Elodie Ferrand maintains that the character of the cheese comes from the airflow and humidity of the caves rather than from any strain of mould peculiar to them.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The caves have been used for ripening cheese since the Middle Ages.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Cheese inoculated with mould grown in a laboratory and ripened in the caves is indistinguishable from cheese made the traditional way, while the same mould used in a warehouse is not.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The mould growing in the caves has been given a species name of its own.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The milk for the cheeses comes from a single local breed of sheep.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Raghavan's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The Indus valley seals carry short strings of signs that nobody can read, and it has been argued that they are not writing at all but emblems of office or ownership. Computational linguist Priya Raghavan maintains that the sequences behave statistically like a script encoding a language.

choices.content: Fewer than five hundred distinct signs have been catalogued in total.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The longest sequence yet recovered contains seventeen signs.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The probability of one sign following another falls in the range found in known scripts and far outside the range found in non-linguistic sign systems such as heraldic emblems.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain the obstacle the imaging had to overcome. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Several hundred papyrus scrolls were carbonised by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE.
  • Attempts to unroll them physically in the eighteenth century destroyed many of them.
  • X-ray tomography records the internal shape of a rolled scroll without opening it.
  • The carbon ink is very nearly the same density as the carbonised papyrus it sits on.
  • Models trained to find the faint surface texture the ink leaves have recovered readable Greek.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Several hundred papyrus scrolls were carbonised by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Because the carbon ink is nearly the same density as the carbonised papyrus beneath it, the scans had to be read by models trained to pick out the faint texture the ink leaves.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Attempts to unroll the scrolls physically in the eighteenth century destroyed many of them.

choices.label: D
choices.content: X-ray tomography records the internal shape of a rolled scroll without opening it.

  • Its walls are stacked from basalt columns, some of them weighing several tonnes.
  • The basalt outcrops lie on the far side of the island from the site.
  • The builders had no wheel, no draught animal and no metal tool.
  • Oral tradition on Pohnpei says the stones were flown into place by sorcery.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Oral tradition on Pohnpei holds that the stones were flown into place by sorcery.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The builders moved basalt columns weighing several tonnes from outcrops on the far side of the island, without the wheel, draught animals or metal tools.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The walls of Nan Madol are stacked from columns of basalt.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Nan Madol is a complex of nearly a hundred artificial islets built in a lagoon off Pohnpei.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Lead poisoning is the leading cause of death among released condors.
  • Every free-flying condor is trapped twice a year, tested, and treated if its blood lead is high.
  • California banned lead ammunition for all hunting in 2019.
  • Blood lead levels in the wild flock have fallen since the ban but remain above the threshold in many birds.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Lead poisoning is the leading cause of death among released condors.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The California condor swallows fragments of metal when it feeds on a carcass shot with lead ammunition.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Since California banned lead ammunition in 2019, blood lead levels in the wild flock have fallen, but many birds still test above the threshold.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Every free-flying condor is trapped twice a year and tested for lead.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “bloom” most nearly mean?

questions.passage: Iron smelted in a bloomery never melts. choices.label: B

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A carillon bell is cast too thick on purpose and then cut away. Any bell sounds five notes at once, and the intervals between them are fixed by the profile of the wall rather than by the size of the bell. The founder mounts the casting on a lathe and turns metal off the inside, testing after every pass, until the five partials fall into tune with one another. Metal taken off cannot be put back, so the whole procedure runs one way only, from a sharp bell towards a flat one.

choices.content: It follows a single founder through the casting of one bell.

choices.label: B

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.content: To explain why one lookout's observation cannot by itself locate a fire.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING

questions.subject: READING_WRITING

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Oyelaran's argument?

questions.stem: The student wants to emphasise that the distortion of the map was deliberate rather than a defect. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Harry Beck drew a new map of the London Underground in 1931, in his own time.
  • He straightened every line to a horizontal, a vertical or a 45-degree diagonal.
  • Distances on his map bear no fixed relation to distances on the ground.
  • The publicity department first rejected the design as too radical.
  • A trial printing of 750,000 copies in 1933 sold out within a month.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Beck straightened every line to a horizontal, a vertical or a 45-degree diagonal, accepting that distances on the map would bear no fixed relation to distances on the ground.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The publicity department first rejected Beck's design as too radical.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A trial printing of 750,000 copies sold out within a month in 1933.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Harry Beck drew a new map of the London Underground in 1931, in his own time.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain what made a tally stick hard to forge. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The English Exchequer recorded debts on notched hazel sticks for some six centuries.
  • Each stick was split lengthways, and the payer and the Exchequer kept one half each.
  • The grain of a split stick matches only its own partner.
  • Tally sticks circulated as a form of credit, since a half-stick could be sold on.
  • The accumulated sticks were burned in 1834, and the fire destroyed the Palace of Westminster.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The accumulated sticks were burned in 1834, and the fire destroyed the Palace of Westminster.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The English Exchequer recorded debts on notched hazel sticks for some six centuries.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Tally sticks circulated as a form of credit, because a half-stick could be sold on to somebody else.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A tally was split lengthways and the two halves kept apart, and the grain of a split stick matches only its own partner.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the pillar has not rusted while modern iron would. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The iron pillar at Delhi was forged about 400 CE and stands seven metres high.
  • It carries almost no rust after sixteen centuries in the open air.
  • The iron contains an unusually high proportion of phosphorus.
  • A thin film of iron hydrogen phosphate hydrate forms on the surface and seals it.
  • Modern iron is made with the phosphorus removed, because phosphorus makes steel brittle.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The pillar's high phosphorus content produces a sealing film of iron hydrogen phosphate hydrate, whereas modern iron has the phosphorus taken out because it makes steel brittle.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The pillar carries almost no rust after sixteen centuries in the open air.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Modern iron is made with the phosphorus removed, because phosphorus makes steel brittle.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The iron pillar at Delhi was forged about 400 CE and stands seven metres high.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An overloaded ship rides low, and a sea that would run along the deck of a light vessel comes aboard instead. <u>The mark painted on the hull is not a limit on cargo but a limit on how deep the hull may sit in the water.</u> The same ship may load until the line reaches the surface in one sea and must stop short of it in another, because water of a different temperature and salinity lifts a hull differently. The tonnage the mark permits therefore changes with the voyage.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It describes the procedure by which the mark is painted on a hull.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It draws a distinction that the rest of the text goes on to develop.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It concedes that shipowners frequently ignored the mark.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It explains why timber is a particularly dangerous cargo to carry.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An Athenian jury was not chosen by anybody. Each citizen willing to serve pushed a bronze ticket into one of the columns of slots cut in a stone slab, and a tube fixed at the side was loaded with black and white balls. A crank let one ball fall at a time; a white ball sent a whole row of ticket-holders onto the jury and a black one sent the row home. The machine settled nothing about who was fit to judge. It settled only that no official had picked them.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To describe a mechanism and identify the narrow question it was built to settle.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that Athenian juries reached sounder verdicts than modern ones.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To trace the growth of Athenian democracy across the fifth century.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To explain how the bronze tickets were manufactured and inscribed.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Cahokia, on the flood plain opposite present-day St Louis, held more people around 1100 than London did. Its central mound was raised basketload by basketload and covers more ground than the Great Pyramid. Within two centuries the plazas stood empty. Excavation has turned up no siege line, no mass grave and no single burnt layer; what it shows is a city that drew people in from several regions and then, across decades, let them go again.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Cahokia was destroyed in a war whose traces have not yet been located.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Cahokia was a large city that emptied gradually rather than in a single catastrophe.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Cahokia's central mound is the largest earthwork ever raised anywhere.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Cahokia's population was drawn entirely from the surrounding flood plain.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A limb that has been amputated can go on hurting, and patients often describe the pain as a hand clenched too tightly to open. Vilayanur Ramachandran stood a mirror upright between a patient's arms so that the reflection of the intact hand appeared where the missing one had been. Patients asked to open both hands watched the missing hand open. For some the cramp eased at once, and for a few it did not come back.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The mirror restored feeling to the amputated limb itself.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Giving patients a visual image of the missing hand moving relieved pain for some of them.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Phantom pain is caused by damage to the nerve endings that remain in the stump.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Every patient who used the mirror was permanently cured of the pain.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Duarte's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Aircraft flying over the Petén forest fire laser pulses through gaps in the canopy and time their return, building a model of the ground under the trees. choices.label: B
choices.content: Laser pulses do not reach the ground where the canopy is completely unbroken.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Many lowland Maya cities were abandoned during the ninth century.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The laser models show house platforms, causeways and field walls spread across areas that ground survey had recorded as empty forest.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Teo's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Several rainforest trees in northern Queensland bear fruit the size of a fist, with a stone too large for any other animal in the forest to swallow whole, and a seed that germinates poorly where it falls. Ecologist Marion Teo argues that these trees now depend on the cassowary for dispersal to a degree that puts them at risk.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Cassowaries also eat fungi, insects and small animals.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Seedlings of these trees are found at any distance from a parent tree only in forest where cassowaries still range, and nowhere else.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Cassowary numbers have fallen as roads have been cut through the forest.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The fruit of these trees is brightly coloured when ripe.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Moretti's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Ten thousand murex snails yield a few grams of dye, and the colour deepens with age instead of fading. Historian Silvia Moretti argues that the price of Tyrian purple was set by the labour of collection rather than by any secret held by the dyers of Tyre.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Roman law reserved the deepest shades of purple for the emperor and his household.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The chemistry of the dye was not worked out until the twentieth century.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Vats of decomposing snails smelled so foul that dyeworks were kept outside the city walls.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Workshops far from Tyre produced dye of the same quality as soon as the snails were available to them, and charged as much for it.

questions.passage: A gecko's toe is covered in half a million hairs, each splitting at the tip into hundreds finer still, and the animal hangs from polished glass by one foot. choices.content: the roughness of the surface being climbed.

choices.label: B
choices.content: the extremely close contact of the split hairs with the surface.

choices.label: C
choices.content: air pressure acting on the underside of the toe.

choices.label: D
choices.content: a fluid secreted by the pads of the toe.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An atomic clock keeps a second defined by a transition in caesium, and that interval does not vary. The rotation of the Earth does vary: tides, the movement of the atmosphere and the slow rebound of land once buried under ice all change the length of a day by a millisecond or two. Civil time is held in step with the sky by inserting an extra second whenever the two have drifted a second apart. That these insertions are needed at unpredictable intervals shows that what is irregular is _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: the caesium transition on which the second is defined.

choices.label: C
choices.content: the tides raised by the moon and nothing else.

choices.label: D
choices.content: the accuracy of the clocks making the comparison.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why greenhouse growers came to depend on bumblebees. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The anthers of a tomato flower release pollen only through a small pore at the tip.
  • A bumblebee grips the anther and vibrates its flight muscles without moving its wings.
  • The vibration shakes the pollen out through the pore.
  • Honeybees cannot produce the vibration.
  • Greenhouse growers pollinated tomato flowers by hand until commercial bumblebee colonies became available in the late 1980s.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The anthers of a tomato flower release pollen only through a small pore at the tip.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Honeybees cannot produce the vibration that shakes pollen from a tomato anther.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Commercial bumblebee colonies became available to greenhouse growers in the late 1980s.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A bumblebee vibrates its flight muscles to shake pollen out through the pore of a tomato anther, which honeybees cannot do; growers who had pollinated by hand turned to bumblebee colonies from the late 1980s.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the species survives without recovering. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The American chestnut made up a quarter of the hardwood canopy in parts of the Appalachians.
  • A fungus introduced about 1904 killed some four billion trees within fifty years.
  • The fungus kills the trunk but not the root system, which goes on sending up shoots.
  • The shoots die back before they are old enough to set seed.
  • Breeders cross surviving trees with the blight-resistant Chinese chestnut and back-cross the offspring to American parents.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The American chestnut once made up a quarter of the hardwood canopy in parts of the Appalachians.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A fungus introduced about 1904 killed some four billion American chestnut trees within fifty years.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The fungus kills the trunk but not the root system, so shoots keep coming up and then die back before they are old enough to set seed.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Breeders cross surviving trees with the blight-resistant Chinese chestnut and back-cross the offspring to American parents.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why Nancarrow wrote for the player piano. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Conlon Nancarrow wrote music for the player piano from the late 1940s onward.
  • A player piano reads holes punched in a paper roll rather than a performer's hands.
  • He punched the rolls himself, one hole at a time, on a machine he had built.
  • The studies layer tempos in ratios such as 17:18 that no two human players can hold together.
  • Only a handful of the studies were heard outside his Mexico City studio for thirty years.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Because his studies layer tempos in ratios such as 17:18 that no two performers can hold together, Nancarrow wrote for a machine that reads punched holes instead of writing for players.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Only a handful of Nancarrow's studies were heard outside his Mexico City studio for thirty years.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A player piano reads holes punched in a paper roll rather than a performer's hands.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Nancarrow wrote for the player piano from the late 1940s and punched every roll himself, one hole at a time.

questions.stem: An apiary sells jars of blossom honey for $9 each and jars of heather honey for $14 each. At one market it sold 5 more jars of blossom honey than of heather honey and took $436 from honey sales altogether. How many jars of heather honey did the apiary sell?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The number of metres the balloon descends each minute.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The number of metres above the ground at which the descent begins.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The number of minutes the balloon takes to reach the ground.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The number of metres above the ground after 1,200 minutes.

questions.stem: A horticulturist randomly assigned 240 seedlings of a single variety to two mulches and found that the seedlings grown under bark mulch grew significantly taller, on average, than those grown under straw mulch. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
questions.subject: MATH

choices.label: A
choices.content: The difference in growth was caused by the kind of mulch, for seedlings like those in the study.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Bark mulch makes any plant grow taller than straw mulch does.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The difference in growth cannot have been caused by the kind of mulch.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Every seedling of this variety grows taller under bark mulch than under straw mulch.
